answer: The sparrow multiplier is published, charged in karst, and summit lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4624 identities would post 829 proofs and burn roughly 5 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
